svg.title: The CH347T development board in mode 1: its headers, the chip pins behind them, and what atiic drives
svg.text: LXC-CH347 (CH347T board) in mode 1: the headers
Top view, USB-C left. Each header: its silkscreen, the chip pin behind it, its function in mode 1, and its pins() name.
the same chip pin as another header
An SPI display (ST7735, GC9A01), as run
• In mode 1 the UART0 and JTAG headers are mode 0's and mode 3's names: the same chip pins as the SPI and I2C headers (dashed).
• Wire to the SPI and I2C headers, and leave the dashed ones free: a wire there sits on the bus too.
• The back labels IO0-IO7: mode 0's GPIO numbers. In mode 1 WCH's driver offers IO4, IO6, IO7 only; the rest are SPI's and I2C's.
• GPIO7 (UART1 RTS) and UART1 DTR carry the mode switch: GPIO7 is driven only if S1 pulls it through a resistor.
• UART1 (TX, RX) is the serial port, ttyACM on Linux. 5V is USB's, 3V3 the board's 3.3 V: the displays and the MPU-6050 ran from it.

Headers from the vendor's photos, front and back; chip pins from the silkscreen names and WCH CH347DS1 V1.6 (§4.3), borne out by the back's IO labels; GPIOs per WCH's Linux driver. atiic docs/ch347.md.
